justification: Three guards against a session-behaviour failure that cost an hour on 2026-08-17. No product code and no served output changes - this is developer tooling. Standard rather than Minor because two of the three BLOCK a tool call, so a false positive would stop work, and because the whole point is that they must fire on the real case and not on ordinary commands.

falsifiable_check.command: TOOL_INPUT='{"command":"git push 2>&1 | grep error"}' python .claude/hooks/push-retry-needs-full-output.py   (twice, then unfiltered)
falsifiable_check.fails_when: NOT SELF-REFERENTIAL: each guard is exercised against the ACTUAL files and commands from the incident, and required to separate them. The new-file guard must BLOCK frontend-nextjs/scripts/verify-solar-delivered.tsx (the throwaway that was committed) while ALLOWING frontend-nextjs/lib/solar/delivered.ts, scripts/check_control_subject_mismatch.py and scripts/fixes/dq84_exclude_misfiled_controls.py - all real, all created the same day. A guard that blocks all four, or none, fails. The retry guard must allow the first filtered push, block the second at the same unpushed sha, and allow an unfiltered one.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Observed in both directions, not asserted. New-file guard, run against the four real files: 4 of 4 correct. Its FIRST version was wrong and was caught this way - searching for the bare stem, it passed lib/solar/delivered.ts because two January strategy documents under .claude/docs/history/ contain the word 'delivered'. A guard satisfied by prose is not looking for a caller; tightened to the basename and the parent/stem import path. Retry guard: attempt 1 filtered exits 0, attempt 2 at the same sha exits 2 with the message, an unfiltered push exits 0. Both guards exit 0 on `ls -la`.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The evidence is the repository, not this code: git grep decides whether anything references a file, and the remote-tracking ref decides whether the previous push landed. Neither is a claim the hook makes about itself, which is the point - the escape the prior-art guard offers is a written sentence, and that sentence was supplied three times on 08-17 while the habit continued.

pre_impl.existing_data: The Sol round cap ALREADY EXISTED at 3, added by #967 on 2026-08-16. Its counter for fix/solar-dc-vs-delivered read 1 - so the reviewer blocked ONCE and the cap never fired. Meanwhile 5 of that branch's 9 commits were `chore(qa): restamp`. The cap was not the binding constraint, and lowering it alone would not have prevented the incident.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The whole diagnosis was wrong twice. First I blamed the adversarial reviewer for looping; the counter says it blocked once. Then I blamed the QA-report stamp treadmill; that was real but not what failed the pushes either. The actual cause was that every push command ended in `| grep -aE 'error:|QA-GATE: FAILED'`, which printed the failure HEADER and cut off the line beneath it naming the error - a single `=== null`. Six attempts on a filter that could only confirm my own hypothesis.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Two new hook files, both wired into the existing PreToolUse[Bash] chain beside pre-commit-gate.py rather than into a new mechanism. The cap change is one number in an existing block. Deliberately NOT a written rule: prose guidance was given and broken four times the same day, and the repo's own memory records that prose rules fail within hours while gated ones hold.

functions.name: main (push-retry-needs-full-output.py)
functions.what: Counts push attempts per branch and HEAD sha, and blocks a SECOND attempt at the same unpushed sha when the command filters its own output.
functions.input: TOOL_INPUT env var, JSON carrying the Bash command about to run
functions.output: exit 0 to allow, exit 2 to block with a message on stderr
functions.if_none: If the branch, HEAD or repo root cannot be resolved it exits 0. It never blocks on ignorance - a guard that fires when it cannot tell gets switched off.
functions.edge_cases: `cd "<path>" && git push` is resolved to that directory, because this repo runs everything from worktrees and reading the session's project dir would count another branch's attempts. --no-verify is left alone: an explicit emergency bypass is its own decision. The counter resets when origin/<branch> contains HEAD, so a successful push clears it.
functions.failure_mode: At worst it asks for one unfiltered push. It cannot let a bad push through, because it never permits anything the other hooks would refuse.

functions.name: main (no-unreferenced-new-file.py)
functions.what: Blocks `git commit` when a newly ADDED file is named nowhere else in the repository - the signature of a file written to answer a question rather than to change the product.
functions.input: TOOL_INPUT env var; reads the staged add-list from git
functions.output: exit 0 to allow, exit 2 listing the unreferenced files
functions.if_none: No staged additions, or none outside the exempt paths, exits 0.
functions.edge_cases: Tests, migrations, docs, .qa/, .claude/, .github/ and data-ish suffixes are exempt - they are found by convention, not by being named, and blocking them would make the hook fire on ordinary work. The search deliberately excludes .claude/docs/history/, whose archived prose made the first version pass a file on the word 'delivered'. A QA report mentioning the script it was written for does not count as a caller.
functions.failure_mode: A genuinely new module committed BEFORE its first caller is blocked. That is the intended trade: give it a caller, or a ledger entry, in the same commit. The remedy is stated in the message.

break_it.scenario: A push fails, and the retry is run with the same output filter that hid the reason the first time.
break_it.what_happens: This is the incident. Six attempts, each showing 'QA-GATE: FAILED' and cutting off the line that named the error, each followed by a fix for the wrong thing.
break_it.how: The second attempt at the same unpushed sha is blocked when the command pipes to grep/head/tail/awk/sed. The message names the command and tells the operator to re-run it bare, or to ask the gate directly.
break_it.repro: TOOL_INPUT='{"command":"git push | grep error"}' python .claude/hooks/push-retry-needs-full-output.py   # run twice

break_it.scenario: The guard fires on the first push of every branch, or on ordinary commands.
break_it.what_happens: It becomes noise, and a hook that fires constantly gets bypassed - which this repo has already recorded as the reason the Sol block is scoped narrowly rather than applied to everything.
break_it.how: Only a REPEATED attempt at the same sha is blocked, and only when the command actually filters. Verified: `ls -la` exits 0, the first filtered push exits 0, an unfiltered push always exits 0.

break_it.scenario: A real new module is committed and the new-file guard blocks it - for example lib/solar/delivered.ts, or a DQ check script.
break_it.what_happens: Legitimate work is stopped and the guard gets disabled.
break_it.how: Tested against the four real files created on 08-17: the throwaway is blocked, the shared module (imported by four surfaces) and the two check scripts (named in .claude/dq_checks.json) are allowed. 4 of 4. A new module committed with its caller, or a check committed with its ledger row, passes - because git grep reads the working tree, so the staged reference is already visible.
break_it.repro: on fix/solar-dc-vs-delivered: stage the shared solar module and commit - allowed; stage frontend-nextjs/scripts/verify-solar-delivered.tsx - blocked

break_it.scenario: Someone assumes the lowered Sol cap is what fixes the looping.
break_it.what_happens: The wrong lever gets pulled again. Measured on the branch in question: the Sol counter was 1, and the repeated cycle was output filtering plus the QA restamp, neither of which the cap touches.
break_it.how: The cap block in .githooks/pre-push now carries that measurement inline, so the next person to look at the number reads what it did and did not cause before changing it.

post_merge.db_reset: No database access, no schema change, nothing written.
post_merge.watch: If either guard blocks work that is plainly legitimate, say so rather than working around it - a bypassed guard is worse than none, and the exemption lists in both files are meant to be extended.
post_merge.manual_verify: Run the two repro commands above. The retry guard must allow, then block, then allow-unfiltered. For the new-file guard, the four files it was calibrated on live on OTHER branches (fix/solar-dc-vs-delivered and fix/control-subject-mismatch), so re-run it there: it must block verify-solar-delivered.tsx and allow the shared solar module plus both DQ check scripts.
